title: Vacancies
description: Recruitment section with open positions, vacancy cards, details modal, and response CTA.

runtime: shared modal system handling data-modal-id and data-modal-close

variants.title: Split aside
variants.description: Intro and response CTA on the left, vacancy card grid on the right.
variants.usage: Use when the section is a two-column recruitment layout with title/description and response CTA separated from the vacancy card list.
acceptance: Rendered section has .vacancies.vacancies--split-aside.
The aside contains the section header and the response CTA.
The aside header uses .section-header.section-header--column-start for a left-aligned vertical title/text stack.
On mobile, split-aside initializes the vacancies Swiper with slidesPerView auto, 12px spaceBetween, neutral 320px cards, and no visual skin tied to Swiper active state.
The vacancy cards render in a two-column desktop grid and become a horizontal slider strip on mobile.

variants.title: Grid CTA
variants.description: Top section header, wide vacancy card grid, and centered response CTA below.
variants.usage: Use when the section is a full-width recruitment layout with header above the card grid and the response CTA below it.
acceptance: Rendered section has .vacancies.vacancies--grid-cta.
The section header renders above the cards without block-specific header layout overrides.
Vacancy cards reveal the visible "Читать полностью" action on hover/focus.
On mobile, grid-cta initializes the vacancies Swiper with slidesPerView auto, 12px spaceBetween, 350px cards, visible "Читать полностью" action, and a centered response CTA block.
The vacancy cards render in a three-column desktop grid and the response CTA renders below the grid.

aliases.purpose: Legacy names from existing projects. Agents use these only to find and map old implementations; new code must use the canonical naming fields.

agent.usage: Use this block only for recruitment/open-positions sections where the data and interaction are vacancy-specific: position title, experience, schedule, pay, details modal, and response CTA. If a future section only reuses the visual card layout without this recruitment contract, choose or create another semantic block instead.
transferSteps: Choose a variant by matching the target design structure, not by brand colors.
Copy section-vacancies.blade.php as the target section view unless the project has an explicit naming map.
Ensure required foundation styles, button partial, and shared modal runtime exist before adding block-specific SCSS and JS.
Ensure Swiper and FreeMode are available when using the mobile vacancy card strip; initialize it only on max-width 767px and destroy it on wider screens.
Add a vacancies:vacancies collection fixture or map an existing legacy key through the target CMS layer.
Keep one modalVacancy instance; populate it from each card's .vacancy-card__modal-content via vacancies.js.
Keep modalVacancy markup in the vacancies section view immediately after the section; do not move it to foundation, page layout, or duplicate it per card.
Route response CTAs through modalContact instead of duplicating vacancy forms inside every card.
Use theme/foundation tokens for brand skin differences; do not create brand-specific variants for colors, radii, fonts, or button skins.
acceptance: Rendered section has the canonical .vacancies class and one supported variant modifier.
Rendered target-project section uses id="vacancies" and aria-labelledby="vacancies-title" regardless of selected variant.
Rendered vacancy cards use .vacancy-card and read title, text, pay, exp, and work_time from vacancies:vacancies items.
Exactly one modalVacancy exists for the section.
modalVacancy markup is block-owned and remains in the vacancies section view, while modalContact is only referenced as a shared/global modal.
Clicking a .vacancy-card__hitarea fills modalVacancy from .vacancy-card__modal-content.
Injected vacancy description content is styled by raw CMS tags inside .vacancy-modal__description: p, h1-h6, ul, ol, and li must not require extra CMS classes.
Response CTAs target modalContact.
Button elements use foundation button styles without block-specific button size, padding, radius, icon, hover, active, or typography overrides.

Block-specific SCSS does not target or override .section, .container, .section-header, .section-title, .section-text, or .button as standalone selectors; left-aligned vertical headers use foundation .section-header--column-start.
Both variant demos visually mirror the shared Blade structure.
notes: Canonical section ids stay semantic: use id="vacancies" and aria-labelledby="vacancies-title" in target projects.
Variant names describe layout and belong in modifiers such as .vacancies--split-aside or .vacancies--grid-cta, not in section ids.
Demo HTML may use preview-only unique ids only because multiple variants render on the same registry page.
agent.futureGeneralization: If a non-vacancy section later shares the card-to-details-modal-to-CTA scenario, extract a shared base block such as detail-card-list and keep vacancies as a domain preset or compatibility layer.
